newsitem.title: GERMANY: Buba member Koebnick may leave post-state official.
newsitem.headline: Buba member Koebnick may leave post-state official.

text.p: Bundesbank council member Hans-Juergen Koebnick may be leaving his position this year as part of a local government shakeup, a parliamentary deputy in the state of Rhineland-Palatinate said on Wednesday.

"Koebnick will go back to the Saar (state) where he came from and take up a position as head of a banking federation. His planned move is a part of a broader shakeup in governor Kurt Beck's Rhineland government," Herbert Jullien, a member of the opposition Christian Democrats told Reuters.

A spokesman for Koebnick, who is also president of the state central bank in Rhineland-Palatinate and the Saar region, declined to comment directly on the story. "Koebnick has said this is a rumour and I do not comment about rumours," he said.
Koebnick, a member of the Social Democrats and formerly Lord Mayor in Saarbruecken, joined the central bank council in 1993 for an eight-year term, becoming well known to markets.
Jullien said Gernot Mittler, finance minister in the state of Rhineland Palatinate, is considered to be a leading candidate as successor to Koebnick in the job as central bank president.
"Mittler is a banker and has an idea of what is going on while Koebnick has no financial background at all," he said.

Some independent economists have said state central bank presidents may soon begin looking around for other jobs as their positions, while maintained, would be severely limited once the Bundesbank hands over its policy-making function to the European central bank.
